families.title: Fabric Covered Panel Skins To The Floor
families.subtitle: For Panel Buildups
standardIncludes: Panel skins, fabric direction application, if selected: fabric price group 1
requiredToSpecify: 2 Fabric color number for skin surface
tips: Tip: Remember to omit base trim(s) on a horizontal frame package when using a skin to the floor.
Tip: 48"H and 60"H fabric covered panel skins accommodate fabric in the vertical direction only.
Tip: 72"W fabric covered panel skins accommodate fabric in the horizontal direction only.
Tip: For further information about fabric direction, see page 713.
Tip: 30"H and 42"H skins only work on junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011.

Tip: When specifying skins, the total skin height will be 6" less than the panel height. When ordering skins to the floor an F suffix will be added to the end of the style number for the skin in the lowest position on the panel. The total skin height will still be 6" less than the panel height. See Panel Buildups, page 12, for more information.
notes: TKF = tackable acoustical to the floor; TAF = performance tackable acoustical to the floor.
No 60"H x 72"W to-the-floor skin is offered (TS76072TKF / TS76072TAF not printed; Statement of Line p.102 shows 60"H 72"W as standard only).

The 48"H/60"H vertical-only tip applies to the to-the-floor skins (page 107: '60" high to the floor skins can only accommodate fabric in the vertical direction'; '48" high to the floor skins only accommodate fabric in the vertical direction').
For Canadian Pricing: Multiply U.S. Price by the Canadian price factor. See page 1 for details.

rules.text: Total skin height on a panel = panel height - 6". Example: 54"H panel -> 48" of total skin height. Applies to all skin types (fabric, steel, markerboard, laminate, wood). See Panel Buildups, page 12.

To-the-floor skins: an F suffix is added to the end of the style number of the skin in the LOWEST position on the panel. The total skin height is still panel height - 6" (54"H panel -> 48" of skin height specified).
Skins sized to go to the floor extend to the bottom of the panel; they can be used on one or both sides of the panel; they can only be used in the bottom position.
Omit base trim option should be selected on the panel frame (horizontal frame package) when using a skin to the floor (pages 107,108,110,114,115,436,439,445,448,454).

Standard height skins are not dedicated to a specific location. Skins extend onto the junction and meet the skin of the adjacent panel; the slotted channel of the junction is accessible between these two skins. Skins can be removed and repositioned.
18"H, 30"H, and 42"H fabric skins only work on junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011 (to-the-floor fabric page 436: 30"H and 42"H).
18"H and 30"H steel skins only work on junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011 (steel to-the-floor page 439: 30"H).
18"H and 30"H markerboard skins (standard and to-the-floor) only work on junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011.
18"H slatwall skins only work on junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011.
18"H, 30"H, and 42"H laminate skins only work on junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011 (laminate to-the-floor page 445: 30"H and 42"H).
18"H, 30"H, and 42"H wood skins (standard and to-the-floor) only work on junctions manufactured on or after October 10, 2011.

Fabric skins (tackable TK and performance tackable TA): heights 12,18,24,30,36,42,48,60"H x widths 18,24,30,36,42,48,60,72"W all available. To-the-floor (F) sizes: 24-60"H in all widths EXCEPT 60"H x 72"W (standard only).
Steel skins: 12,18,24,30,36"H x 18-72"W (18,24,30,36,42,48,60,72). To-the-floor: 24,30,36"H all widths. 12"H, 18"H and 24"H steel skins are available with ribbed and perforated steel option.
Ribbed and perforated steel option not available on to the floor size skins.
Markerboard skins: 12,18,24,30,36"H x 18,24,30,36,42,48,60,72"W; to-the-floor 24,30,36"H all widths.
Slatwall skins: 12,18,24"H x 24,30,36,42,48"W only; no to-the-floor.
Wood skins: 12-60"H x 24,30,36,42,48"W; to-the-floor 24-60"H; wood skin sets (S) exist for total skin heights 36,42,48,60" (i.e. 42", 48", 54", and 66" panel heights), standard and to-the-floor.
Markerboard surfaces for steel skins: 12,24,36"H x 24,30,36,42,48"W only.

Fabric application is standard in the warp horizontal direction; warp vertical direction is available as an option (no cost) on 18"W to 60"W skins. Exceptions: 72" wide standard and to-the-floor skins can only accommodate fabric in the horizontal direction; 60" high to-the-floor skins can only accommodate fabric in the vertical direction; 48" high to-the-floor skins only accommodate fabric in the vertical direction. See Specification Guidelines for Directional Fabrics, page 713.
Performance tackable acoustical skins have a sound-blocking barrier added to the back side.

Power and communication can be accessed by cutting a fabric skin in the field. Templates for receptacle and communication cutouts available from Service Parts (T500940SR). Filler to close unwanted cutout available from Service Parts (TS7STFSR). Face plate (ordered separately) surrounds a receptacle / modular furniture size communication outlet when field-cutting fabric skins.

NEMA-size communication outlets can be installed on the face of a panel skin without a face plate (screws only); order from an outside vendor. NEMA-size communication outlets cannot be used in the base.
Powerkits are available in widths that correspond to panel widths.
Power and communication cannot be accessed in steel skins; steel skins cannot accommodate power receptacles or communication outlets - use the base or a fabric skin for power access.
Ribbed option is available on 12"H, 18"H, and 24"H panels (skins) only. Perforated option is available on 12"H, 18"H, and 24"H only.

Horizontal connecting bars / horizontal beam and back of opposite skin are visible through perforated skin. When specifying the perforated option, order perforated skins for both sides of the panel to maximize the visual aesthetic.
Perforated skins cannot be used in installation with steel or ribbed steel skins made prior to July 10, 2000.

Steel paint price groups by height tier 12"H to 24"H / 30"H / 36"H: PG1 no cost; PG2 +$22/+$22/+$45; PG3 +$38/+$38/+$75. Ribbed steel +$22 (12-24"H only). Perforated steel per-row price (12-24"H only). To-the-floor (439): 24"H to 30"H / 36"H: PG2 +$22/+$45, PG3 +$38/+$75.

Markerboard surface adheres to steel skins via a magnetic border; order steel skin of the same size to support it. Markerboard surface can span multiple skins; can be removed and repositioned. Not for use on steel panels with the ribbed surface. White only. Dry erase markers only.
Markerboard skin is steel construction and accepts magnets; white only. Power and communication cannot be accessed in markerboard skins.
Slatwall skins have horizontal channels supporting Details worktools and accessories on 1" increments. Maximum load on skin is 80 pounds.
Power and cables cannot be accessed in a slatwall skin.
Back-to-back slatwall skins cannot be installed at the top of a panel when using a ceiling access lay-in utility package.

Slatwall channels will align when the bottom of a 12"H slatwall skin is adjacent to the bottom of an 18"H or 24"H slatwall skin; they will NOT align when the top of a 12"H slatwall skin is adjacent to the top of an 18"H or 24"H slatwall skin.

Binder bin or shelf can be hung in front of a slatwall skin. If two bins or shelves are hung side by side in front of slatwall skins, the top hook must use either the third or fourth full slot down from the top; the first and second full slots from the top will not accept side-by-side shelves.
Binder bin or shelf can be upmounted on slatwall skin as long as there is not another bin or another slatwall skin on the adjacent in-line panel.
Slatwall skins cannot be hung next to a cantilever or on module end panel.
Slatwall skins cannot span a stacked joint.
Slatwall skins cannot be used in the bottom 12" of an Answer panel.
Off-module worksurface to panel connector cannot be used in front of or on the adjacent panel at the same elevation as a 12"H or 24"H slatwall skin.
Slatwall skin brace package is required when mounting a Details flat panel monitor arm on an Answer slatwall skin.

One Details single or dual monitor arm can be mounted on a 12"H slatwall skin that has an installed brace package. Up to two Details single monitor arms can be mounted on an 18"H or 24"H slatwall skin that has an installed brace package. Optimal stability area: 6" in from each side, 3" from top, 4" from bottom of skin.

Laminate skins: laminate surface captured by painted metal trim border on all sides; non-tackable; can be used in monolithic applications or in combination with other skin types on the same frame. Power and communication cannot be accessed in laminate skins. Open Line laminate option +$65 plus cost of laminate.

Wood skins: wood veneer captured by painted metal trim border on all sides; non-tackable; grain of wood veneer cathedrals runs vertically. Individual wood skins can be used monolithic or combined with other skin types on the same frame. Power and communication cannot be accessed in wood skins. Options: Premium wood 2, Premium wood 3 (per-size upcharge), Customiz stain (no cost).

Wood skin sets contain specific combinations of sizes and are used when segmenting all wood skins on 42"H, 48"H, 54"H, or 66"H panels; the use of sets ensures correct cathedral wood grain alignment of all segmented skins on a frame.

Set compositions (panel height: set = skins top to bottom): 42"H A=12+24; 48"H A=12+30, B=18+24; 54"H A=24+24, B=12+12+24, C=12+36; 66"H A=12+12+12+24, B=12+24+24, C=12+12+36. Widths 24,30,36,42,48". WSS = standard, WSF = to the floor.

Steel technology skins: 6,12,18"H x 24,30,36,42,48,60,72"W. Markerboard technology skins: 12,18"H x 24-48"W. Slatwall technology skins: 12,18"H x 24-48"W. 12"H and 18"H technology skins are available with ribbed steel; technology skins available with fabric-covered option.

Technology skins 30" or under are available with all cutouts or with only right- or left-hand cutouts. 60"W and 72"W skins have double cutouts and can be optioned to have them on both sides, right hand only or left hand only. 6"H technology skin has an option to omit all cutouts.
Technology cover is specified separately and accommodates a receptacle and a NEMA or DECORA communication port. Number of technology covers specified must match the number of cutouts in a skin.

Slatwall technology skins include a painted trim for each cutout used behind the technology cover, painted to match the skin. Slatwall technology skins must follow the same vertical placement rules as slatwall skins (page 112-113).

Technology skin surface materials: 6"H - painted steel, fabric covered steel (option); 12"H and 18"H - painted steel, ribbed steel (option), fabric covered steel (option), slatwall-painted, markerboard. Technology cover colors: 6000 Black, 6009 Arctic White, 6249 Platinum Solid, 6654 Sand, 6697 Fog.
Standard modular powerkits must be used with technology skins and covers; they cannot be used with hardwire kits.

Communication ports can never be back-to-back. 24"W technology skins have one cutout; communication can only be accommodated on one side of the panel at the same elevation. All 36"W, 42"W, 48"W technology skins have one or two cutouts: right-hand cutout accommodates power only or power and communication, left-hand cutout power only. All 30"W, 60"W, 72"W technology skins have one or two cutouts; for each double cutout the right-hand opening accommodates power only or power and communication, left-hand power only.
If using powerkits shipped prior to April 2000 in an existing application, power and communication cover must be placed on the left-hand side of the technology skin.

Technology skin cover fillers are available to allow the technology skin cover to work with technology skins manufactured before October 10, 2011; fillers available for single or double cutouts and are painted.

6"H technology skin can only be used in the position just above the worksurface; includes powerkit brackets to reposition the powerkit location on the junction. When a 6"H technology skin is used on one side (worksurface height), a 12" or 18" technology skin cannot be used on the opposite side at the same location. 6"H technology skins cannot be used on a 30" high panel. 6"H technology skins with no cutouts can be used in any 6" position except the bottom 12" of the panel.

Slatwall skin brace package is required when mounting a Details flat panel monitor arm on an Answer slatwall technology skin. One Details single monitor arm can be mounted on a 12"H or 18"H slatwall technology skin with a single cutout; the skin must have an installed brace package.

Receptacle cover available through Service Parts (891700204MP) if no receptacle is specified. Technology cover includes all adapters/fillers for power-only and power+communication, and a filler if no communication is used.

Glass windows single pane and single pane kits for custom glass: 12,18,24"H x 24,30,36,42,48,60,72,78,84,90,96"W. Double pane: 12"H x all widths 24-96"W; 18"H and 24"H x 24-72"W only. Tackboard for use with wall channels: 18"H x 24,30,36,42,48,60,72"W.

Glass window cannot be used at the base of a panel. 12"H, 18"H, 24"H glass windows can be placed in the top position by stacking junctions or by lowering the top horizontal connecting bar (24" maximum) in the base panel.

No more than two windows may be stacked on top of each other. A 24"H glass window installed in the top of a base panel cannot accommodate any windows stacked on top. Tackable acoustical skins and steel skins can be stacked.

Power and cables cannot be routed vertically or accessed in a glass window. Top channel of a window in the top position can accommodate lay-in cable routing beneath the top cap. Hanging components cannot be hung in front of a double-pane window.
Surface materials: frame paint; single-pane 6500 Clear Glass or 6530 Frosted Glass; double-pane 6530 Frosted Glass only. Safety glass provided unless custom glass window kit is ordered.

Hanging components cannot be used next to a double-pane window at a 90 degree corner. Open design upmount bin and shelf bracket cannot be used when a double-pane window is in top position of panel. Sliding panel door cannot be used when a double-pane window is used in the host panel.

A single glass window can span two or more in-line panels; spanning windows should be used in the top position only; same-size spanning top cap recommended; spanning window in-line support must be specified separately (one at each in-line junction). Spanning windows of any width cannot be stacked. When double stacking junctions, at least one stacking junction must be connected with a horizontal beam.

When ordering a 78"W or wider single pane window kit to be used with steel or fabric skins located directly below it, two clips (T521328SR) should be ordered and installed. Windows slide into junctions from the top and require ceiling clearance above the panel. Custom glass kits accommodate 4 mm - 6 mm glass (max thickness 0.245").
Sliding panel door: 36"W and 42"W x 66"H and 78"H.

Sliding door is handed; right-handed or left-handed must be specified. Left-hand door closes right to left (lock on right-hand side); right-hand door closes left to right (lock on left-hand side). Lock option available; specify lock cylinder and key separately. Door must be installed on the outside of the workstation.

Door height must match host panel height (66"H or 78"H); receiving panel height must match door height. Match host panel width to door width if possible. Door is not freestanding; attached to host panel only; track attaches to host and opposite panel.

If a host and/or receiving panel run exceeds 4', a junction stabilizer bracket must be applied to the door end of the host and/or receiving panel run. On long runs apply a junction stabilizer bracket or perpendicular panel every 8'. Sliding panel door cannot attach to a host panel with a double-pane window. Insert: standard 6625 Translucent (ribbed plastic); options 6500 Clear glass, 6541 White laminated.
Fence connectors 32 1/2"H x 2"D; fence vertical post tube 16"H; posts (X-post, Y-post) 33"H x 4"D; beams 8 1/2"H x 3'4", 4', 5', 6', 7', 8', 9', 10'W.

Fence connector is handed (left or right side of frame), occupies vertical slots 32 1/2" up from bottom of base trim, mounted within the module width of the frame; horizontal space within that frame is reduced by 1 1/4" (affects panel-mounted worksurface width). Monolithic skins and lower segmented skins up to 32 1/2" from bottom of base trim are trapped by the fence connector; base trim is not trapped.

Cantilevers cannot occupy the same vertical slots as the fence connector bracket. Fence connector cannot be used when panels are stacked and loaded with bins and shelves. Fence connector cannot be placed between two slatwall skins.

Minimum beam length 4', maximum 10'. Beams may be field cut; anchor block drilling fixture from Service Parts (946800102SR). Posts attach to beams in in-line, L-, T-, X-, or Y- (120 degree) configurations; 3" leveling between post and base extension; height-adjustment jack Service Parts 946800103SR; post base shims ordered separately. Large post base 8 1/2" dia, small 4 1/2" dia. Screen attachment hardware to Post and Beam ordered separately. Fence dust covers 10-foot lengths, field-cut.

Surface materials: fence connector 8043 Clear Anodized aluminum only; post top cap 6694 Slate plastic only; vertical post tube 6644 Fusion Dark plastic only. Shelves on fence 35 1/4" high. Tether brackets as side supports reduce horizontal space by 1 1/2" each side.
